assessments.reasoning: Printed p. 49 explains the receiver result in the spend example despite its final assignment. Printed p. 50 depicts the up-arrow for returning the expression’s value and shows the assignment-as-operand and conditional-return cases.

challenge.method: Compare the last ordinary assignment, direct up-arrow assignment, nested conditional returns on printed pp. 50–51, and successful primitive versus fallback on p. 52.
challenge.results: Ordinary completion in the spend example returns the receiver. Prefixing the assignment with the printed return operator produces the assigned value after storing it. A chosen conditional branch can return from the surrounding method. A successful primitive is a separate completion path, and an escaped block’s attempted return is outside the proposition.

limitations: The two reviewed cases are ordinary body completion and a return taking effect from that method. Primitive outcomes, ordinary block results, and expired home activations are separate scopes.
Direct documentary review of the 1983 edition. No Smalltalk runtime was used.
